This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act 1989 against respondents for seeking
compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02.  The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:-
That on 19-02-2022 at about 07.15 p.m, when the petitioner was going towards his Village Nagalapura from Kolar by travelling in a Honda Activa Scooter bearing No.KA-01-HJ-8261 as a pillion rider, ridden by his friend Madhuchandra, when they were proceeding in front of Shiva Hotel, on the two-wheeler lane of Kolar - Bengaluru NH-75 Road, near Maderahalli Village Gate, Kolar Taluk and District, one Maruthi Swift Dzire Car bearing No.KA-04-ML-6285 was passing beside the above said scooter on its right side of the road, driven by its driver, at high speed, in rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden swerved his car towards left side of the road to go towards ESSAR Petrol Bunk, without observing other vehicles on the road and without any indication or signal.
As a result the driver of the car lost control over his vehicle and the said car dashed against the Motor Cycle of the petitioner.

Due to this the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately taken to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical hospital, Kolar and he was admitted in the hospital twice and has undergone surgery and till today he is under treatment as an outpatient and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc., and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 34 years and was interior designer by profession and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.

entities.text: Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical hospital, Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to accidental injuries he is bedridden and lost his income.
The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Car.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. Owner, the respondent No.2 being the insurance policy holder and the respondent No.3 being the insurer of the said offending Car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- together with interest and costs.
03. On service of summons, the respondent No.3 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

Inspite of service of summons, the respondents No.1 and 2 remained absent and hence,
they were placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.3 in its written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued insurance policy bearing No.0516023120P113745272 valid from 24.02.2021 to 24.02.2022 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to validity of driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle and also terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further denied age, avocation, income of the petitioner, manner of accident and nature of the injuries Umashankar.C vs B.N. Dhananjaya on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96451393/
2 sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.

The driver of the Car did not have valid and effective driving licence to drive the same on the date of accident and the Car did not have valid permit and fitness certificate on the date of accident and hence this respondent is not liable to compensate the petitioner and the rider of the two- wheeler did not have valid and effective driving licence to ride two-wheeler on the date of accident and the accident took place due to rash and negligent riding of the two-wheeler.

The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.3.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 19.02.2022 at about 07.15 p.m, in front of Shiva Hotel, near Maderahalli Village Gate, on Kolar-Bengaluru NH-75 Road, Kolar Taluk and District,
due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Maruthi Swift Car bearing registration No.KA-04-ML-6285 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02 . Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03
. What Order or Award?

06. In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined the doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability as PW.2 and got marked 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16 and closed petitioner side evidence.
However, the respondent No.3 has not lead its evidence.
Hence, respondent No.3 evidence is taken as nil.

07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for petitioner and despite sufficient opportunity was given to respondent No.3, it has not advanced its arguments, hence respondent No.3 arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 As per final order  for the following:

3
09. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.3 counsel, but nothing has been brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

10. Further, PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained left knee fracture proximal tibia, tenderness,
swelling, deformity of left knee, cut lacerated wound over left leg and decreased toe movements of left foot due to foot drop and he assessed disability for left lower limb at 60% which is 20% to the whole body and he also stated that petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants and correction of foot drop with tendon transfer costing approximately Rs.3,00,000/- and he has produced Recent clinical examination notes, Disability evaluation form, Inpatient admission card and X-ray as per Ex.P.13 to 16.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.3 counsel he stated that next day of the accident they have conducted the surgery and admits that fractures are united and denied to the suggestion that the petitioner is diabetic and had high blood pressure and denied to the suggestion that second time surgery was not conducted and it is only cleaning and he voluntaries that it is not cleaning but it is surgery and admits that petitioner as of know has not used external supporting aparatis.
11. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Kolar Rural Police against driver of the offending Car.
Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint lodged against driver of the offending Car for his rash and negligent driving and caused the accident.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of IMV report shows involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Wound certificate of the petitioner which indicates that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Ex.P.6 is Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of the offending car for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.

Ex. P.7 is Discharge summary issued by Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical hospital, Kolar, which discloses that petitioner was admitted as inpatient from 19.02.2022 and discharged on 24.02.2022 for 06 days due to accidental injuries.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex.P.8 is another Discharge summary of same hospital, which discloses that petitioner was admitted as inpatient from 05.04.2022 and discharged on 18.04.2022 for 14 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.9 is Diagnostic report.
Ex.P.13 is Recent clinical examination notes.
Ex.P.14 is Disability evaluation form.
Ex. P.15 is Inpatient admission card and Ex.P.16 is X-ray.

12. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioner, which clearly establishes that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 19-02-2022 at about 07.15 p.m, in front of Shiva Hotel, on Kolar - Bengaluru NH-75 Road, near Maderahalli Village Gate, Kolar Taluk and District, due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Swift Dzire Car bearing No.KA-04-ML-6285, by its driver as alleged in the petition.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved the Issue No.1.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

4 13.
Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.
The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 34 years and was interior designer by profession and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.

Due to accidental injuries he is bedridden and lost his income and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc.,.
14.

It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth and he has not produced any evidence regarding his avocation and income.
But he has produced Ex.P.11 copy of Aadhaar card.

Eventhough the said Aadhaar card is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of cogent evidence with respect to date of birth of petitioner, the said document can be relied upon, according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 20.06.1985 and the alleged accident occurred on 19.02.2022.

Therefore,
it appears that as on the date of accident the age of petitioner is 37 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 37 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 36 to 40 years is 15.
15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As discussed above, with regard to avocation and income the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2022 to be taken as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,500/-.

16. According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained left knee fracture proximal tibia, tenderness, swelling, deformity of left knee, cut lacerated wound over left leg and decreased toe movements of left foot due to foot drop and he assessed disability for left lower limb at 60% which is 20% to the whole body.
However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 20%.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 and 8 Discharge summaries, according to which the petitioner was admitted twice at Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic hospital as inpatient for total period of 20 days.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Umashankar.C vs B.N. Dhananjaya on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96451393/
5 18.
Pain and sufferings:-

As per Ex.P.5 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and Ex.P.9 Diagnostic report, Ex.P.13 Recent clinical examination notes, Ex.P.14 Disability evaluation form, Ex.P.15 Inpatient admission card and Ex.P.16 X-ray and on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
19. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,500/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 20 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 04 months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.62,000/-
(Rs.15,500 x 4) under this head.
20. Medical expenses:- As per Ex.P.12 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.2,50,545/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,50,545/- under the head of medical expenses.

21. Loss of future amenities in life and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness,
the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
22. Future medical expenses:-
According to PW.2 doctor the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants and correction of foot drop with tendon transfer costing approximately will be Rs.3,00,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation with regard to future medical expenses.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
23. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount  No. in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 5,58,000-00
2 . Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00
3 . Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges

4. Medical Expenses 2,50,545-00  5. Loss of future amenities in 30,000-00  life and unhappiness  6. Loss of income during laid up 62,000-00  period  7. Future medical expenses 30,000-00  Total 9,90,545-00

Umashankar.C vs B.N. Dhananjaya on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96451393/
6 24.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,90,545/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

25. Regarding liability:- In this case the respondent No.3 has taken several defences in its written statement, but even despite sufficient opportunity has been given to the respondent No.3, it has not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and there is no evidence on record to show that the driver or the owner of the offending vehicle have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further, the respondent No.3 in its written statement at para 2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending Car and the same is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.
Further, the respondents No.1 and 2 were remained absent and placed exparte.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. Owner, the respondent No.2 being the insurance policy holder and the respondent No.3 being the insurer of the said offending Car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.3 being the insurer shall liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.9,90,545/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) within two months from the date of this Judgment.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,90,545/- (Rupees Nine lakhs ninety thousand five hundred and forty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.3 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,90,545/- (Rupees Nine lakhs ninety thousand five hundred and forty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.3 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
